description: The PEP standard CGE models are a family of open computable general equilibrium models from the Partnership for Economic Policy for simulating how macroeconomic shocks and policies affect sectors, institutions, poverty and welfare. PEP-1-1 is a static single-country model with several categories of labour and capital, PEP-1-t its recursive dynamic version, PEP-w-1 a single-period multi-region world model, PEP-w-t its recursive dynamic version, which uses the GTAP 8.1 data base in version 4.1, and PEP-w-t-fin a dynamic world model with international financial assets in a bilateral structure. They were written by Bernard Decaluwé, André Lemelin, Véronique Robichaud and Hélène Maisonnave for PEP's macro-micro modelling group. Coverage is any national economy with a social accounting matrix, or the world, with a 14-region, 4-commodity aggregation of GTAP data distributed with GTAP's permission. The GAMS code, user guides and presentations are available free under a Creative Commons licence. Caveats: users need GAMS and must build their own data, and the pages read do not give release dates for all versions. For simulation they model how a price or supply shock to one sector spreads through an economy and trade partners, including financial flows, supporting resilience studies of industry, agriculture and finance. It is related to the GTAP standard model record in this catalogue.
